title: Fix config authority load boundary
summary: Separated ordinary PSD1 config reads from active settings-authority loading, and made settings-authority PSD1 imports fail strictly on timeout or parse failure instead of promoting defaults from an empty mapping.
reason: The desktop backend test suite exposed a config load failure where a PowerShell import timeout was swallowed as `{}`, then the settings store tried to promote default settings and failed during projection validation. The same boundary also risked routing profile/snapshot PSD1 reads through the per-user authority store.
behavior_before: `load_config_data()` routed all PSD1 reads through the per-user JSON settings authority. Import timeouts could be treated as empty settings input, and profile/snapshot reads could ignore the PSD1 file they were asked to load.
behavior_after: `load_config_data()` performs direct PSD1 reads for profiles, snapshots, and compatibility callers. Active path resolution uses `load_settings_authority()` when available, and settings-authority imports raise `SettingsStoreError` on timeout/failure without writing a default store.
